questions.def: 'Will' is used for predictions about the future.
questions.question: I think it ___ rain later.

questions.def: Scheduled events use 'is scheduled to start'.
questions.question: The meeting ___ at 9 AM tomorrow.

questions.def: Scheduled events can use the present simple tense.
questions.question: The train ___ at 6:30 tomorrow morning.

questions.def: 'Will' is used to ask about future plans.
questions.question: ___ you be using your car tonight?

questions.def: Future perfect for an action completed before another future action.
questions.question: By the time you arrive, I ___ dinner.

questions.def: Future perfect continuous for duration up to a point in the future.
questions.question: They ___ on this project for three months by July.

questions.def: Type 1 conditional: present simple after 'if'.
questions.question: If it ___, we will stay inside.

questions.def: Reported speech: 'will' changes to 'would'.
questions.question: He said he ___ me back.

questions.def: Tag question should match 'going to'. Should be 'aren't she?'
questions.question: She is going to fly to Paris next week, isn't she?

questions.def: 'Are doing' for plans. Be + V-ing.
questions.question: What ___ you ___ this weekend?

questions.def: 'Will call' = immediate future action after arriving.
questions.question: I ___ you as soon as I arrive.

questions.def: Scheduled events often use the present simple.
questions.question: The film ___ at 7 PM sharp.

questions.def: Planned arrangement: 'am meeting'.
questions.question: I ___ him tomorrow afternoon.

questions.def: 'Are going to' expresses intention or prediction.
questions.question: We ___ have to leave soon.

questions.def: Future continuous for an action in progress.
questions.question: This time next week, I ___ on a beach!

questions.def: Future perfect: completed before a point in future.
questions.question: By 5 PM, he ___ all his work.

questions.def: 'Are planning' expresses a future intention.
questions.question: They ___ to build a new stadium.

questions.def: 'Will be' is used for future states and predictions.
questions.question: I think I ___ a doctor.

questions.def: 'Are travelling' suggests a definite plan.
questions.question: We ___ to Italy next summer.

questions.def: Present simple for scheduled events.
questions.question: The concert ___ at 8 PM, so don't be late.

questions.def: 'Should' expresses expectation about the future.
questions.question: He ___ be here by now.

questions.def: 'Is going to' for immediate predictions based on evidence.
questions.question: It looks like it ___.

questions.def: 'Will let' is the most natural way to promise information.
questions.question: I ___ you know as soon as I hear anything.

questions.def: 'Will' is the most common auxiliary for future continuous.
questions.question: We ___ be having dinner when you arrive.

questions.def: Future perfect indicates completion before a future time.
questions.question: By the time you arrive, I ___ all my work.

questions.def: Present continuous for planned future arrangement.
questions.question: I ___ my friend tomorrow afternoon.

questions.def: Simple present for scheduled events.
questions.question: The meeting ___ at 10 AM tomorrow.

questions.def: "Will" for predictions and opinions.
questions.question: I think it ___ rain later today.

questions.def: "Be bound to" expresses strong probability.
questions.question: She ___ be angry when she finds out.

questions.def: Future perfect for completion before a time.
questions.question: By next year, I ___ to many countries.
